headline: 66% of people approve of PM Tarique Rahman in new survey
summary: While the Prime Minister enjoys strong personal popularity, a Doplar Opinion Research survey shows the government faces significant pressure over energy and price hikes.
details: A survey by Doplar Opinion Research, marking six months of the BNP government, reveals that 66.30% of respondents believe Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is performing his duties well.

The Prime Minister's approval is consistent across age, gender, education, and income levels, with support even from supporters of Jamaat-e-Islami (65.50%), NCP (65.80%), and the Awami League (52.50%).
However, overall government performance is viewed more critically, with 54.50% approval compared to 32.90% who say the government is performing poorly.
The survey highlights severe public dissatisfaction with energy management, with 89.40% rating it as poor, while 69.10% are unhappy with the prices of essential commodities.
Regarding the country's direction, 48.60% believe Bangladesh is on the right path, while 35.60% feel it is going in the wrong direction.
On a social level, 95.20% of people feel safe practicing their religion openly, and 67.50% feel safe walking alone in the dark in their own neighborhoods.
The survey also found that 78.60% support the government's Family Card project and 70.70% support its tax policies.
The research involved 3,443 participants from 489 wards and villages across 64 districts, based on a previous study by InnoVision Consulting.
caption:
66% of Bangladeshis approve of PM Tarique Rahman, but the government is struggling with energy and prices.

A survey by Doplar Opinion Research, marking six months of the BNP government, reveals that 66.30% of respondents believe Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is performing his duties well.

The Prime Minister's approval is consistent across age, gender, education, and income levels, with support even from supporters of Jamaat-e-Islami (65.50%), NCP (65.80%), and the Awami League (52.50%).

However, overall government performance is viewed more critically, with 54.50% approval compared to 32.90% who say the government is performing poorly.

The survey highlights severe public dissatisfaction with energy management, with 89.40% rating it as poor, while 69.10% are unhappy with the prices of essential commodities.

Regarding the country's direction, 48.60% believe Bangladesh is on the right path, while 35.60% feel it is going in the wrong direction.

On a social level, 95.20% of people feel safe practicing their religion openly, and 67.50% feel safe walking alone in the dark in their own neighborhoods.

The survey also found that 78.60% support the government's Family Card project and 70.70% support its tax policies.

The research involved 3,443 participants from 489 wards and villages across 64 districts, based on a previous study by InnoVision Consulting.

headline: Bangladesh Presidential polls set for Thursday
summary: Chief Election Commissioner says all preparations are complete for the election, while a court rejects a plea to stay the schedule.
details: The presidential election in Bangladesh is scheduled to take place this Thursday. The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) has confirmed that all necessary preparations for the polls have been completed.
A writ petition seeking to stay the election schedule was recently filed in court, but the plea was dismissed, clearing the way for the vote to proceed as planned.
The CEC noted that while the country may not be accustomed to frequent presidential elections, the commission is fully prepared to manage the process.
The Chief Whip has described the upcoming election as the start of a new journey in the nation's history.
caption:
Presidential polls are coming this Thursday. All preparations are complete and legal challenges have been cleared.

The presidential election in Bangladesh is scheduled to take place this Thursday. The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) has confirmed that all necessary preparations for the polls have been completed.

A writ petition seeking to stay the election schedule was recently filed in court, but the plea was dismissed, clearing the way for the vote to proceed as planned.

The CEC noted that while the country may not be accustomed to frequent presidential elections, the commission is fully prepared to manage the process.

The Chief Whip has described the upcoming election as the start of a new journey in the nation's history.
